quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #14
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 19

questions.question: Another driver is trying to pass your car. What should you do?

options.text: Pull off the road.
Signal to the other driver when it is safe for them to pass.
Check for oncoming traffic and slow down to let them pass safely.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for oncoming traffic and slow down to let them pass safely.
questions.explanation: Stay in the right lane when another driver passes you on the left. Look for oncoming traffic and reduce your speed so the other car can move back into the right lane safely.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle is using its siren and flashing lights. What must you do immediately?

options.text: Pull to the right and stop.
Pull to the right and slow down.
Pull to the right and turn on your four-way flashers.
Stop and let the emergency vehicle pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle uses its lights or sirens, you must drive to the right side of the road and stop immediately.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and get ready to stop if other cars are coming.
Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
Go through the intersection slowly without always stopping.
Stop only if traffic is on the crossing road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A stop sign means you must come to a complete stop. Let vehicles and pedestrians in or near the intersection go first. Then go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this black and yellow sign mean?

options.text: The road to the right has one-way traffic only.
There is a detour to the right because of roadwork.
Slow down because the road ahead makes a sharp turn.
There is a crossroad to your right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down because the road ahead makes a sharp turn.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead turns sharply (in this case, to the right). Slow down as much as you would when turning at an intersection.

questions.question: What does a steady yellow light at an intersection mean?

options.text: Go.
Yield to other cars.
Slow down and get ready to stop.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and get ready to stop.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a red light is coming soon. Slow down and prepare to stop. If you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely, go through carefully.

questions.question: Driving while distracted:

options.text: Is never dangerous.
Usually makes drivers react more slowly to hazards.
Usually makes drivers go faster.
Is only dangerous for young drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually makes drivers react more slowly to hazards.
questions.explanation: Distractions slow down how fast a driver can react to traffic and hazards. Distracted driving is always unsafe.

questions.question: How often is a state vehicle inspection required?

options.text: Only if the vehicle is older than 10 years.
Every year.
Every two years.
Only when you buy the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every year.
questions.explanation: West Virginia requires all vehicles to have a yearly inspection to make sure they are safe to drive.

questions.question: When do pedestrians have the right-of-way?

options.text: At an intersection.
When crossing an alley or driveway.
If they are using a cane.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right-of-way at intersections and crosswalks. They also have the right-of-way when crossing alleys or driveways. Blind pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog always have the right-of-way.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn allowed.
You must turn right.
Watch for traffic on your right.
Do not park on the right side of the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn allowed.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a line through a symbol means that action is not allowed. In this case, the symbol shows a right turn is not allowed.

questions.question: When turning left, you must yield the right-of-way to:

options.text: Other drivers already in the intersection.
Oncoming traffic.
Pedestrians already in the intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to oncoming traffic. Always yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.question: You see a flashing red light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
Stop only if other cars are also approaching.
Stop only if other cars are already in the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop, let other traffic pass, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: You are driving slowly and traffic is backing up behind you. What should you do?

options.text: Drive even more slowly.
Pull over to the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
Don't let the other cars pass your vehicle.
Turn on your four-way flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is dangerous. If traffic backs up behind you on a two-lane road, pull over to the right and let other vehicles pass.

questions.question: What must you do when you see a flashing red traffic signal ahead?

options.text: Slow down at the light.
Drive through carefully without stopping.
Move to the right lane.
Stop before you enter the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before you enter the intersection.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must stop. Let other traffic and pedestrians pass. Go only when it is safe. At a railroad crossing, a flashing red light warns that a train is coming. Wait until the lights stop flashing and all warning devices are off before you go.

questions.question: Two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The vehicle coming from the right.
The vehicle coming from the left.
The driver who honks first.
The vehicle traveling faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle coming from the right.
questions.explanation: When two similar vehicles meet at an intersection with no traffic control signs, the vehicle coming from the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: Where is parking prohibited?

options.text: Within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.
Within 50 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection.
Within 100 feet of the nearest rail at a railroad crossing.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.
questions.explanation: Parking is not allowed within 15 feet of a fire hydrant, within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection, or within 50 feet of railroad tracks. Always park only where it is legal and safe.

questions.question: Where should your car be positioned before making a right turn?

options.text: Near the center of the street.
On the left side of the street.
On the right side of the street.
Past the center of the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the right side of the street.
questions.explanation: Before turning right, move as far to the right side of the road as possible. Never cut across other lanes to make a turn.

questions.question: What can happen to a bicyclist who breaks traffic laws?

options.text: Nothing, because bicyclists don't have to follow traffic laws.
They can be given a ticket.
They will always get a warning from police.
Their bicycle will be taken away.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can be given a ticket.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights, duties, and responsibilities as car drivers. Both drivers and bicyclists can be ticketed for breaking traffic laws.

questions.question: What does a green arrow traffic signal mean?

options.text: It is used only on one-way streets.
It means go, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
It only works if there is also a circular green light.
It shows the way to an airport.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means go, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go, just like a circular green light. However, you must turn in the direction the arrow is pointing.

questions.question: When it starts to snow or sleet, what should you do?

options.text: Keep your windshield and mirrors clear.
Stay farther away from the vehicle in front of you.
Drive carefully near all other vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: In snow and ice, keep your windshield and mirrors clear. Increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead because slippery roads make it harder to stop.

questions.question: When can you legally pass another vehicle on the right?

options.text: When the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is a passing lane available.
Even if you have to drive off the road.
On a narrow bridge.
Anytime you want to.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is a passing lane available.
questions.explanation: You may pass on the right when there is an available passing lane and the vehicle is turning left or about to turn left. You can also pass on the right on a multilane road with two or more lanes in the same direction. Never drive off the road to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: If a train is coming and could be dangerous, what must you do?

options.text: Slow down and go carefully.
Do not cross the tracks until the train has passed completely.
Cross the tracks at your own risk.
Find another route to cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not cross the tracks until the train has passed completely.
questions.explanation: Always look and listen for trains before crossing railroad tracks. If a train is near or moving fast enough to be dangerous, you cannot cross. This applies even if there are no signals or the signals are broken.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Turn right after stopping completely.
You cannot turn right.
You can turn left.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot turn right.
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign. It shows a law that all drivers must follow. Right turns are not allowed where this sign is posted.

questions.question: Can you drive around or under a gate that is moving at a railroad crossing?

options.text: Yes, if the train is not too close.
Yes, if your car will not hit the gate.
Yes, if you look both ways first.
No, never.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights, lowered gates, and bells at a railroad crossing mean you must stop completely. Do not cross until the lights and bells stop and the gates are fully up. Never drive around or under a moving gate.

questions.question: At a light rail intersection, what should you always do?

options.text: Look both ways before crossing the tracks.
Pay attention and follow all traffic signals.
Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists.
All of these.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these.
questions.explanation: Never drive around lowered gates. Always look both ways before crossing train tracks and obey all signs and signals. Trains share the road with cars and bicyclists.

questions.question: A fire engine is following you on a two-lane street without using its emergency lights or siren. What should you do?

options.text: Keep driving normally.
Stop as fast as you can.
Speed up to move out of the way.
Slow down, move right as far as possible, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep driving normally.
questions.explanation: If an emergency vehicle is following you without its siren or flashing lights on, you do not need to move or stop. Continue driving normally.
